answer: The “father of the father of psychoanalysis” was **Jakob (Jacob) Kolloman Freud** (1815 – 1896). He was the biological father of Sigmund Freud, the founder of psychoanalysis. Jakob was a wool merchant and a member of a Hasidic‑Jewish family that was part of the Jewish Enlightenment (Haskalah). He married three times and had 10 children, including Sigmund. His life and relationship with his son influenced some of Freud’s early ideas about the father complex and family dynamics.
